messages:
perf-alert-bot: Evening perf alert: p95 latency for serving-runtime/model-std jumped from 78ms -> 210ms around 02:10 UTC. Throughput steady. :warning:
perf-alert-bot: Dashboard: https://graf.redwood/alerts/5001239876 (slo: 100ms)
perf-alert-bot: Top hint: kernel-selector change + larger batching window correlated with spike.
maria: seen it, thanks. getting CI perf job link now. :eyes:
ci-bot: CI perf job failed: perf-test/runner-104 - 02:12 UTC - regressions detected (p95 +165%). Logs: https://ci.redwood/jobs/104
ash: who merged the selector/batching PR last night?
yousef: that was M3452 by devon — it bumped selector epsilon and increased max_batch_ms to 12ms.
devon: yep, M3452. intent was to reduce cold-start token cost. didn't run the perf regression suite against long-tail workloads (my bad).
lucy: repro locally on my devbox with a synthetic tail workload. p95 jumps when batch stride increases beyond ~8ms.
maria: can we bisect quickly? if it's M3452 we should hold the rollout.
yousef: starting quick git-bisect across the last 6 merges. will narrow to commit in ~10min.
sre-bot: Canary rollout paused for service serving-runtime in us-east-1 due to SLA breach.
ash: thank you. keep canary paused — no automatic rollforward.
ash: devon, please prepare a revert PR if bisect confirms.
devon: on it. also running a profiler to check kernel selection counts. small flame snippet below:
```
Kernel selector counts (sample):
  stream_kernel_v2: 4200
  poly_kernel: 1500 -> increased to 5400 after M3452
  fast_kernel: 3600
```

maria: poly_kernel increase matches the latency shift. why did selector prefer poly_kernel more?
yousef: selector epsilon change increased probability of picking poly for mid-length sequences; poly has higher p95 on our hardware for these shapes.
lucy: KV cache miss rate also rose ~12% at the same time, likely due to batching stride causing evictions.
ci-bot: perf-test/runner-104 traces: top cause appears to be combined effect: kernel choice + cache thrash.
manual: quick mitigation: lower max_batch_ms to 6ms and revert selector epsilon to previous value. can we hotfix config in dedicated pools?
sre-bot: we can push config override to canary nodes; preparing patch.
yousef: applying override to canary now: `selector.epsilon=0.12 -> 0.08`, `batch.max_ms=12 -> 6`.
perf-alert-bot: Canary p95 back to 95ms after override (10min after): https://graf.redwood/canary/5001239876
maria: nice. still need a proper revert + test. devon, can you open revert PR and include targeted perf test for long-tail sequences + KV hotset?
devon: will open PR in 15m. including perf job and a small synthetic replay harness.
nash: action items:
- devon: revert PR + perf job (ETA 45m)
- yousef + lucy: add regression test for batch stride -> kernel-choice interactions (ETA 2d)
- maria: smoke the canary for 2 hours and then schedule controlled rollout
- sre: keep canary paused and monitor kv miss and kernel counts
maria: also add an eval alert that fires on kernel-selection-distribution shift > 20% so we catch this earlier.
lucy: will add alert and a short doc explaining why poly_kernel is bad for mid-length on our infra.
nash: thanks all. post-mortem will be required if revert doesn't clear. closing loop when PR merges. :thumbsup:
